sections.html:
A Weston owner can go through an agent, a cash buyer or an investor, and the choice mostly comes down to how much time and certainty you need. Most Weston homes sit inside a homeowners' association, so a buyer's timeline often depends on association paperwork as well as financing.

  • Cash sale: no lender appraisal, so closing can be quick once the title is clear and any association documents are in hand.
  • Agent listing: a wider buyer pool, with showings and a loan approval period.
  • Investor sale: the buyer accepts the property in whatever shape it is in.

Write the price, closing date and who covers each closing charge into the contract. Then request the association's payoff or estoppel figures early, since an unpaid assessment can hold up the settlement.

Weston began as a planned development, not an old town. Its 15,000 acres were assembled in the 1950s, a regional approval in 1978 first allowed more than 25,000 dwelling units, and later amendments cut the figure to 17,000. The Indian Trace Community Development District followed in 1981 to finance and manage water and sewer mains, water bodies and arterial roads. The first homes were finished in Windmill Ranch and Country Isles in 1984.

That makes Weston houses comparatively recent, and it means association rules and the district's roads, lakes and utilities are part of what a buyer is evaluating. Residents voted to form their own city, and the Legislature approved the local bill on May 5, 1996. The result is a city that controls its own zoning and permits. Ask the city, not the county, about setbacks, additions and pools, and give buyers the same instruction in writing.

Very likely your sale involves one. Most residences in Weston are in a private development governed by an association, and City Code requires each association to register annually with the City Clerk's Office by the first workday in April.

In gated or private communities the common areas are private property, so the association maintains the infrastructure, roads and landscaping inside. Trees on association property and street trees cannot be removed without a city permit. The city maintains most of the water bodies, though some lakes are privately owned.

  • Ask your association or management company for the current assessment status before you list.
  • Collect the governing documents a buyer will request.
  • Confirm whether any lake, drainage or tree work is pending on your lot.

Homeowners who draw irrigation water from a lake or canal need the consent agreement the city publishes, and the city takes questions at 954-385-2000. A buyer who wants to keep that irrigation should ask you for the agreement.

sections.h2: Permits for work before you sell
sections.html:
A permit problem can surface at the worst moment, when a buyer's inspector walks the yard. Call Weston's Building Code Services and Planning and Zoning staff before any exterior work, and ask what applies to the specific job. Tree removal is the clearest rule: street trees and trees on association property cannot come down without a city permit.

Florida enacted a 2026 exemption for some small projects under $7,500, but it has limits. Electrical, plumbing and structural work still need permits, so assume a permit is needed until Weston staff tells you otherwise.

If you finished a patio, pool deck or addition without a permit, ask the Building Department what it would take to close it out before a buyer's inspector finds it. Cash buyers may accept the risk, but expect them to reduce the offer for it. Keep any final inspection approvals and contractor invoices for permitted work, and hand them over with the rest of your closing folder.

sections.h2: Broward County property taxes and your sale
sections.html:
The county sends the bill, and the state calendar sets the dates.

Broward property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Property assessed at just value
AugustProposed-tax notice mailed
NovemberBills sent; 4 percent early-pay discount
FebruaryDiscount drops to 1 percent
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
June 1Tax certificates sold on unpaid items

When you request a payoff figure, also ask the Broward County tax office for the current bill and any delinquent balance.

For homesteaded owners, Save Our Homes limits yearly assessment growth to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The cap ends when the property changes hands, which resets the property to just value the next January 1, so a Weston buyer can face a higher bill than you paid. An owner-occupant buyer can claim up to $50,000 of homestead exemption through Form DR-501, filed with the county appraiser by March 1. The exemption is lost if the home is rented or stops being the owner's permanent home.

If you will buy another Florida home, portability can move some of your accumulated savings to the new homestead when it is established within three years.

Broward County pays Florida's standard deed tax, $0.70 for each $100 of price. Only Miami-Dade has a separate rate. Everyone on the deed is liable, whoever the contract says will pay.

The clerk charges $5.00 to record the first page and $4.00 for each later page, plus trust fund and technology charges. The final amounts appear on your title agent's settlement statement, which you should compare with the contract before closing.

Weston buyers expect a complete packet. Pull your deed and survey, the association's governing documents and fee schedule, and proof that assessments are current. Add permit records for any pool, patio or addition, and the irrigation consent agreement if you draw from a lake or canal.

Request the association's figures in writing and note when they were issued, since buyers and title agents will want recent numbers. If any tree, lake or drainage work is pending on your lot, say so before the buyer finds it. Candor early keeps a cash offer from shrinking late in the process. If the association needs time to produce its documents, tell the buyer the expected date so the closing schedule reflects it. Delays here are common and rarely fatal, but surprises are.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips in Weston
sections.html:
With no loan involved, nobody orders a lender appraisal or waits on underwriting. Where an association exists, the slowest step is usually the paperwork it supplies, so request it the day you accept an offer.

Then a title agent hunts for liens and drafts the settlement statement. You sign the deed, and the clerk records it. Read every line of the statement first, and ask how and when your proceeds will reach you. If a mortgage is being paid off, the statement should show the payoff amount going to your lender, and any unpaid association balance should appear as a deduction too. Ask the title agent to explain any line you do not recognize before you sign anything.

faqs.q: Do most Weston homes belong to a homeowners' association?
faqs.a: Yes. Most residences in Weston are in a private development governed by an association. Ask yours for assessment status and governing documents before listing.

faqs.q: When did Weston become a city?
faqs.a: The State Legislature approved the local bill enabling incorporation on May 5, 1996. Weston grew from a planned community that began with the 1978 Indian Trace approval.

faqs.q: Can I remove a tree from my Weston lot?
faqs.a: Trees on association property and street trees cannot be removed without a city permit. Call the city before any tree work.

faqs.q: Is there a deed tax when I sell in Weston?
faqs.a: Yes. Florida's deed tax runs $0.70 per $100 of price and is collected by the clerk.

faqs.q: When do Broward County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent that day, and certificates are sold by June 1.
